## The Elliot Chart — A Famous Movie Name

*E.T. the Extra‑Terrestrial* (1982) featured a boy named **Elliott** as the main character.  
The assignment asks us to reproduce the “Elliot” chart, which shows how the name **Elliot** changed over time, including the spike following the movie’s release.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

# Load data
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4names/master/data-raw/names_year/names_year.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(url)

# Filter for the exact spelling "Elliot" 
df_elliot = df[df["name"] == "Elliot"]

# Aggregate total per year for the name "Elliot"
elliot_yearly = df_elliot.groupby("year", as_index=False)["Total"].sum()

# Reproduce the Elliot chart with a reference line at 1982
plot = (
    ggplot(elliot_yearly, aes(x="year", y="Total"))
    + geom_line(color="#e377c2", size=1.2)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=1982, linetype="dashed", color="red", size=1)
    + geom_text(x=1982, y=1500, label="E.T. released (1982)", color="red", hjust="left")
    + scale_x_continuous(format="d")
    + labs(
        title="Popularity of the Name 'Elliot' Over Time",
        subtitle="The name surged after the release of E.T. the Extra‑Terrestrial",
        x="Year",
        y="Number of Babies Named"
    )
    + theme_minimal()
)
plot.show()
```
